revision_binding.reason: Tracked content cannot embed its own containing commit without circular identity.

content.heading: Authority, Ownership, and Relationships
content.purpose: Ensure every governed fact has one canonical owner and every non-owning artifact preserves authority through explicit typed relationships instead of restating truth.

owner_kinds.meaning: Machine-readable governance or product authority intentionally adopted as the canonical owner.
Code, configuration, schema, contract, or test that canonically owns an executable fact under repository authority routing.
A higher-authority KIS source that remains canonical until a governed adoption changes ownership.

relationship_catalog.meaning: The source requires the target authority to be valid or interpretable.
The source is structurally or semantically checked by the target contract or validator.
The source prescribes requirements for the target.
The source restricts permitted values or behavior of the target.
The source chooses among behaviors already permitted by the target authority.
The source translates deterministically to the target representation.
The source is an implementation of target authority.
The source records evidence about the target without becoming its authority.
The source is a generated view of the target and has no write-back authority.
The source points to the target owner without restating the governed fact as new authority.
The source replaces the target while preserving lineage.

rules.statement: Every governed fact MUST have exactly one current canonical owner.
A non-owning MRD or repository artifact MAY summarize or project an owned fact for its audience but MUST reference the canonical owner and MUST NOT redefine the fact as independent authority.
Generated HRDs, indexes, dependency maps, and other META projections MUST remain downstream of their canonical sources and MUST NOT become write-back authority.
Relationships between governed artifacts MUST use the governed relationship vocabulary; ad hoc relationship labels MUST NOT silently create new semantics.
When two sources appear to own the same current fact, kis-op MUST surface the conflict and resolve ownership through the applicable authority order before accepting dependent work.
Supersession MUST preserve the previous owner's stable identity and lineage while making the replacement unambiguous.
